Try clearing a filter.Higher or Lower7♠Showing?Next cardHigher: 8 – ALower: 2 – 6Same rank: jackpot ×12Aces are high. A tie on higher/lower loses.How to playGuess whether the next card is higher or lower than the one showing. Aces are high.Each correct guess grows your pot by ×1.5.Cash out after at least one correct guess to keep the pot. A wrong guess or a tie loses it.Or bet that the next card is the same rank: a 1-in-13 shot that pays ×12 your pot.TipsGuess against the middle: if a 7 shows, higher and lower are close to even.On a 2 or 3, bet higher. On a Queen, King or Ace, bet lower.Cash out while you're ahead. The streak gets riskier the longer it goes.

rules:red-dog.text: CategoryAnyCountry of originAnyPlayersAnyType of gameAnyLuck or skillAnyHow hard to learnAnySort byDefault orderMost popular firstAlphabetical (A–Z)Shortest game first0 gamesNo games match. Try clearing a filter.Red Dog4♣?9♥LowThird cardHighWins on 5, 6, 7 or 84 cards in between = pays 1 to 1Landing on the 4 or the 9 loses. Aces are high.How to playPlace a bet and two cards are dealt. The gap between them is the spread: how many ranks fit in between.You win if the third card lands strictly between the two. Landing on either one loses. Aces are high.The smaller the spread, the bigger the payout:1 card in between5 to 12 card in between4 to 13 card in between2 to 14 or more in between1 to 1Consecutive cards (like 6 and 7) can't have anything between them, so it's a push and you keep your bet.A pair gets a third card straight away. If it matches you win 11 to 1, otherwise it's a push.Raise: after seeing the spread you can add up to your original bet before the third card is dealt.TipsRaise only on a spread of 7 or more. That's where the third card lands between them more than half the time.On a narrow spread (1 or 2) the big payout is tempting, but it wins less than one time in six. Don't add to it.Every hand uses a freshly shuffled deck, so there's nothing to remember from earlier hands.
labels: A 4 and a 9 are dealt; the third card wins if it is a 5, 6, 7 or 8

rules:baccarat.text: CategoryAnyCountry of originAnyPlayersAnyType of gameAnyLuck or skillAnyHow hard to learnAnySort byDefault orderMost popular firstAlphabetical (A–Z)Shortest game first0 gamesNo games match. Try clearing a filter.BaccaratPlayer7♠8♥7 + 8 = 15 → 5Banker4♣5♦4 + 5 = 9 → 9Only the last digit counts. Closest to 9 wins, so Banker wins here.J, Q, K and 10 are worth 0. Aces are 1.How to playYou don't play any cards. Choose a bet, press Deal, and the cards play themselves out by fixed rules.Two hands are dealt: Player and Banker. These are just names, and you can bet on either one whoever you are.Add up a hand and only the last digit counts (15 is 5). The hand closest to 9 wins. 10, J, Q and K are worth 0 and an Ace is 1.If either hand starts on 8 or 9 it's a natural and the round ends. Otherwise a hand may draw a third card, depending on its total. The game does this for you.Player wins1 to 1Banker wins0.95 to 1Tie8 to 1Banker pays a little less because the casino takes a 5% commission, and winnings are rounded down to a whole coin.If the round is a tie, Player and Banker bets are returned. Only a Tie bet wins.TipsBanker is the best bet over time, even with the commission, and Player is close behind.The Tie bet pays 8 to 1 but is the worst bet at the table. It's fun for a flutter, not a plan.There's no skill in the cards, so the only choices are your bet and your bet size. Keep your bets small relative to your coins.
labels: Player holds 7 and 8, totalling 5; Banker holds 4 and 5, totalling 9; Banker wins

rules:crazy-eights.text: CategoryAnyCountry of originAnyPlayersAnyType of gameAnyLuck or skillAnyHow hard to learnAnySort byDefault orderMost popular firstAlphabetical (A–Z)Shortest game first0 gamesNo games match. Try clearing a filter.Crazy EightsTop of the pile7♥Your hand7♠K♥8♣3♦same ranksame suitwild!no matchPlay a card that matches the suit or the number of the top card.An 8 matches anything, and you choose the suit that comes next.Can't play? Draw until you can.How to playYou and the bot get 7 cards each. One card is turned face up to start the pile. The first player to get rid of every card wins.On your turn, play a card that matches the top card's suit or its number. Click a card to play it. Cards you can't play right now are dimmed.8s are wild. You can play one at any time, then choose which suit comes next.If you have nothing to play, press Draw cards. You keep drawing until you pick up a card you can play.If the deck runs out, the pile is reshuffled. If nobody can move at all, the round is a draw and your bet is returned.Win the round to get your bet back plus 1× your bet. Lose and you lose your bet.TipsSave your 8s. They're your escape when nothing else fits, and a good way to finish.When you play an 8, choose the suit you hold the most cards of.Get rid of awkward cards, such as the only one you have in a suit, while you can.Watch the bot's card count. When it gets low, stop saving your 8s and go out.
labels: The top card is 7 of hearts. A 7 of spades matches by rank, a king of hearts by suit, an 8 is wild, and a 3 of diamonds cannot be played

rules:slots.text: CategoryAnyCountry of originAnyPlayersAnyType of gameAnyLuck or skillAnyHow hard to learnAnySort byDefault orderMost popular firstAlphabetical (A–Z)Shortest game first0 gamesNo games match. Try clearing a filter.SlotsOnly the middle line pays.Three Glabbers on it is the jackpot!How to playChoose how much to bet, then press Spin. Your bet is taken and the three reels spin, then stop one by one from left to right.Only the middle line, marked in red, pays. The symbols above and below it are just for looks.Three of the same symbol on the line pays like this. These numbers are how many coins come back for every coin you bet, so your bet is included:: 100× your bet: 40× your bet: 20× your bet: 10× your bet: 6× your bet: 5× your bet Exactly two Gigglers, anywhere on the line: 3× your betOne Giggler on its own pays nothing, and so does anything else.The oddsEvery symbol is shown by the same number of stops on each reel, so the rare ones (the Glabber and the Gleeber) really are rare.Over a very long time the machine pays back about 96 coins for every 100 you bet. The rest is the house's share.A spin pays something about 1 time in 4. Most of those are small wins.TipsIt's all luck. Every spin starts fresh, so a machine is never "due" a win and never "hot".A small bet makes your coins last longer, and a big bet chases the jackpot. Both pay back the same share over time.
labels: Three reels with three Glabbers on the middle line, which is the biggest win, a Giggler, a Gembo and a Gazo above, and a Gloober, a Giggler and a Gembo below

rules:roulette.text: CategoryAnyCountry of originAnyPlayersAnyType of gameAnyLuck or skillAnyHow hard to learnAnySort byDefault orderMost popular firstAlphabetical (A–Z)Shortest game first0 gamesNo games match. Try clearing a filter.Roulette17one number35 to 158two touching17 to 11-12a dozen2 to 1Reda colour1 to 1The more numbers a bet covers, the less it pays.How to playThe wheel has 37 pockets: the numbers 1 to 36, which are red or black, and a green 0. The ball lands in one of them.Choose a chip (1, 5, 10, 25, 100 coins), then tap the table to put chips on the bets you like. Tap again to stack more chips. Undo takes back the last chip and Clear takes them all back.When you're ready, press Spin. Your coins are taken, the wheel spins, and every bet that covers the winning number pays out. Rebet puts last round's bets back on the table.Each bet covers some of the numbers, and the more it covers, the less it pays (your chips come back as well):One number (tap it): 35 to 1. Tap 0 for the green zero.Split (the line between two touching numbers): 17 to 1.Street (the bottom edge of a column of three): 11 to 1.Corner (where four numbers meet): 8 to 1.Six line (the bottom corner between two columns): 5 to 1.Dozens (1-12, 13-24, 25-36) and columns (the 2:1 boxes): 2 to 1.Red or Black, Odd or Even, 1-18 or 19-36: 1 to 1.When the ball lands on 0, every bet on red, black, odd, even, low or high loses. That green 0 is the house's edge.TipsIt's all luck: the wheel has no memory, so a number that hasn't come up for ages is no more likely than any other.Every bet is equally fair over time, so spread small chips for a longer game, or one big bet on a colour for a quick one.Keep an eye on the total on the table. You can't put down more than you have.
labels: Chips on the table: a single number pays 35 to 1, a split 17 to 1, red or black 1 to 1

rules:gin-rummy.text: CategoryAnyCountry of originAnyPlayersAnyType of gameAnyLuck or skillAnyHow hard to learnAnySort byDefault orderMost popular firstAlphabetical (A–Z)Shortest game first0 gamesNo games match. Try clearing a filter.Gin RummySet7♥7♠7♦Run4♣5♣6♣DeadwoodK♠3♦same numberin a row, same suit10 + 3 = 13Group your cards into sets and runs. What's left over is deadwood.Aces count 1, face cards 10, other cards their number.Get your deadwood down to 10 or fewer, then knock.How to playYou and the bot get 10 cards each, and one card is turned up to start the pile. A match is played over several hands. The first player to reach 100 points wins it.Make melds. A set is 3 or 4 cards with the same number. A run is 3 or more cards in a row of the same suit, like 4♣ 5♣ 6♣. Aces are low, so A-2-3 is a run, but Q-K-A is not.Cards that aren't in a meld are deadwood. Aces count 1, face cards 10, and the rest their number. The game always groups your best melds for you and shows your deadwood total.To start, the player who isn't dealing may take the turned-up card or pass. Then the dealer may take it or pass. If both pass, the player who went first draws from the stock.Each turn, draw a card from the stock or take the top card of the pile, then discard one card. You can't throw back the card you just took from the pile.When you've got 10 or fewer deadwood points, you can knock. Click the card you want to discard, then press Knock. The game tells you how many points you would have left over.After a knock, the other player may lay off cards onto your sets and runs, like adding a 5♣ to 2♣ 3♣ 4♣. The game does this for them automatically, in the best way. Then both sides count their leftover deadwood, and you score the difference.Gin means no deadwood at all. You score the other player's deadwood plus 25, and they can't lay anything off.An undercut is when the other player has the same or less deadwood than you after laying off. They score the difference plus 25, so be careful when you knock with a lot left over.If only 2 cards are left in the stock, the hand is a draw and nobody scores. The dealer swaps each hand.When someone reaches 100, the match ends. Both players get 20 for each hand they won, and the winner gets 100 extra.You bet once for the whole match. Win it and your bet comes back with winnings: 2× your bet against the normal bot (1.5× on Easy, 3× on Hard, rounded down to a whole coin). Lose, or press Forfeit match, and you lose your bet. Switching to another game doesn't forfeit, but reloading the page does.The Settings button under the table changes how the next match is played. Your choices are remembered on this device:Bot difficulty. Easy knocks as soon as it can. Normal is a careful, fair bot. Hard also remembers what you throw away. The harder the bot, the more a win pays.Match length. The first player to 50, 100 or 150 points wins.When you can knock. Standard is 10 or fewer. In Oklahoma, the value of the first card turned up in each hand is the most you may have left over (an ace is 1). In Gin only, you can only win a hand by going gin.Double bonuses. The gin and undercut bonuses are worth 50 instead of 25.TipsTake a card from the pile only when it fits a meld. Otherwise draw from the stock, because the pile shows the bot what you want.Throw away high cards that don't fit anything first. A king stuck in your hand costs 10 points.Don't rush to knock with 10. If the bot has little deadwood, you could be undercut. Knocking low is much safer.Watch what the bot picks up from the pile. It's collecting that number or suit, so don't feed it.
labels: A hand with a set of three sevens, a run of 4, 5 and 6 of clubs, and two loose cards, a king and a 3, which count 13 points of deadwood

rules:holdem.text: CategoryAnyCountry of originAnyPlayersAnyType of gameAnyLuck or skillAnyHow hard to learnAnySort byDefault orderMost popular firstAlphabetical (A–Z)Shortest game first0 gamesNo games match. Try clearing a filter.Texas Hold'emYour 2 cardsA♠K♥The 5 shared cardsK♦7♣2♠9♥K♣FlopTurnRiverYour best 5 of the 7 cards: K K K A 9That's Three of a Kind.How to playPress Sit down to put 100 coins on the table. You play against two bots, and they start with 100 too. The coins you have left when you Leave table go back to your balance.Everyone gets 2 private cards. Five more are turned face up in the middle for everyone to share, a few at a time: the flop (3 cards), the turn (1) and the river (1).The marked D is the dealer. The next player puts in a small forced bet (1) and the next one a bigger one (2). These are the blinds, so there's always something to win.There's a round of betting before the flop and after each new card. On your turn you can:Fold to give up the hand. You lose what you've already put in, but nothing more.Check if nobody has bet, to pass without paying.Call to match the bet.Bet or Raise to make the bet bigger.All in to bet as much as you possibly can in one go.Bets are a fixed size: 2 coins before the flop and on the flop, and 4 coins on the turn and river. There can be at most 2 raises in a round.All in skips those limits. It bets straight up to the most the other players can match. If you have the fewest coins at the table, that's every coin you have. If you have more, the extra coins stay safely in your stack. The button shows the amount, and everyone else must call it or fold. Once someone is all in, nobody can bet any more and the rest of the cards are just dealt.When the betting is done, players still in show their cards. Your hand is the best five cards you can make from your 2 plus the 5 shared ones. The best hand wins all the coins in the middle. A tie splits them.If everyone else folds, you win the middle without showing your cards.Nobody can bet more than the player with the fewest coins can match, so there are no side pots. If someone runs out, the rest of the cards are just dealt.Best hands, from strongest to weakestRoyal FlushA K Q J 10, all one suitStraight Flushfive in a row, all one suitFour of a Kindfour cards of one rankFull Housethree of one rank and two of anotherFlushfive cards of one suitStraightfive in a rowThree of a Kindthree cards of one rankTwo Pairtwo different pairsOne Pairtwo cards of one rankHigh Cardnone of the above: the highest card playsTipsBe choosy before the flop. Pairs, two high cards (A, K, Q, J) and two cards of the same suit are good starts. Hands like 7 and 2 are worth folding.Folding isn't losing. A hand you don't play costs you nothing more.Don't chase. Calling bet after bet for one lucky card usually costs more than it wins.The bots never bluff. If a bot raises, it has a good hand. If it only calls, it's usually not that strong.Look at the shared cards for what others might have: three of one suit, or cards in a row, could mean a flush or a straight.When you have a strong hand, bet and raise so the pot grows.Going all in is a big move. Save it for a very strong hand, because a bot will only call one with a strong hand of its own. If you shove with a weak hand and get called, you could lose a lot at once.
labels: Two private cards, A of spades and K of hearts, plus five shared cards K, 7, 2, 9, K make three kings
